rationale:
The frontier is the plaza, and for once I do not have to guess: #158 measured it. Three callers — the lane's plaza band, the families and the east agents — share FIVE places, three FOUNT_STANDS and two PLAZA_BENCHES. Over a laneCap sweep of 10 to 20 the plaza's CHOICES go 28.7 -> 48.6 while its ADMISSIONS go 12.4 -> 17.3; the refused share climbs 56.7% -> 64.4% and every one of them leaves by the `else` onto the quay rail. That is why the plaza's presence is the one east number that will not move (+0.14, t 0.7) and why the town's civic centre holds one or two people while the lane streams past it. Two separate cues, c236 and c246, are the same room: c236 adds that all three stands sit on the roundel's SOUTH arc, every approach comes from the south, and the 90-degree stand at (105.5, 33.5) sits ON the lane corridor at ex2 104-106. So b160 is the bet, it goes first, and it gets 90 minutes: the plaza needs more places, spread off the south arc, and more than one thing to DO once you are there. A visitor sees that in the first ten seconds of the wide shot; a fourth bench does not.

The rung is 2 and I want to be plain about why that is legal rather than comfortable. No advisory signal is showing — mapFlat cleared at #155, the diff mean is 103 and rising, no rung has been held. The last two passes were both 4b, so this is the first of at most two consecutive passes at rung <= 2, and the pass after next must climb to 3 or higher whatever it finds. b160 is rung 2 done at full size — it compounds four systems that already exist (the places, the lane's roll, the families, the corridor) rather than adding a sixth — and rung 2 is the ladder's own stated highest-yield move when the basics are in place. I am not spending the climb on a season or a tile I do not need.

The other four are aimed at the four next-longest-untouched domains and at one recurring fault of mine. b161 is the morning: both lapse hours are ONE TAP from the wide shot, the source comment at courtyard.html:5679 says the morning lands at sunUp+0.5 with the sweeper, the cart and nobody else, and the night holds 6-9. b162 spends c238 and b163 spends c243 and c239 together, since both are things drawWaterMirror does not know about and one brief should own the seam. b164 is c241 and it is the manager's own instrument: stall.mjs does not read row.quota, so the memory gate #153 wired into the runner can fire on every single iteration and never raise a signal in the report I plan from — which is precisely the class of blindness this role exists to close.
